scope: Champagne sweetness terminology in the Brennan's study pack

sources.name: Comite Champagne, Dosage
sources.reading: The category concerns sugar in the finished wine. Extra Brut spans 0 to 6 grams per liter; Brut is below 12; Extra Dry is 12 to 17; Sec is 17 to 32; Demi-Sec is 32 to 50. Brut Nature combines less than 3 grams per liter with no sugar added after the second fermentation.

sources.name: Comite Champagne, French FAQ
sources.reading: The French wording explicitly joins the two Brut Nature conditions with 'et': low final sugar and no added sugar. It describes Extra Brut as between 0 and 6 grams.

editorialInference: Extra Brut and Brut have overlapping sugar ranges, so category names alone cannot rank two actual bottles. The house Champagne itself is Extra Brut; other Extra Brut bottles must not be described as drier than it solely because of that label. Perceived dryness also depends on acidity and the wine's other sensory features.
